name: 3D Modeling
description: Sculpting and constructing digital surfaces — polygon meshes, NURBS, and subdivision surfaces — that form characters, props, and environments. The geometric foundation of the 3D pipeline.

name: Texturing & Shading
description: Painting surface detail — color, roughness, bump, displacement — and defining material responses to light via UV mapping and procedural shaders.

name: Rigging
description: Building the digital skeleton and control systems (joints, IK/FK, blendshapes) that let animators pose characters and creatures.

name: 3D Lighting
description: Placing and tuning virtual lights — key, fill, rim, HDRI image-based lighting — to define mood, depth, and realism in a scene.

name: Rendering
description: Converting 3D scenes to final images: offline ray tracing and path tracing for film, real-time rasterization for games and virtual production.

name: Dynamics & Simulation
description: Physically based animation of cloth, hair, fluids, particles, and destruction using solvers rather than manual keyframing.

name: Motion Tracking
description: Recovering the 3D camera movement from live-action footage so CG elements can be inserted with matching perspective.

name: Match Moving
description: Aligning virtual cameras and geometry to real footage frame-by-frame for seamless CG/live-action integration.

name: CG Integration
description: Merging rendered CG elements into live-action plates with consistent lighting, shadows, and lens characteristics.

name: Particle Effects
description: Simulating dust, smoke, sparks, water, and debris with particle systems for explosions and environmental effects.

name: Crowd Simulation
description: Generating large-scale crowds and armies procedurally via agent-based simulation, used for battles and stadium scenes.

name: Set Extension
description: Digitally extending practical sets and matte paintings into vast environments — cities, landscapes, historical reconstructions.

name: Animation Director
description: Leads the creative vision of an animated production, guiding story, performance, and visual style across the pipeline.

name: Storyboard Artist
description: Draws the pre-visualization of shots — camera, staging, timing — that becomes the blueprint for animation.

name: Layout Artist
description: Establishes shot composition, camera moves, and staging before animation begins.

name: Key Animator
description: Draws or poses the defining keyframes of a character's movement, defining timing and performance.

name: Inbetween Artist
description: Draws the intermediate frames between keyframes to create smooth motion — the bulk of traditional 2D animation labor.

name: Background Artist
description: Paints the environments and backdrops behind animated characters, establishing world and atmosphere.

name: Animation Producer
description: Manages budget, schedule, and crew of an animation production, coordinating studios and delivery.

name: Architectural Drawing
description: The graphic language of design — plans, sections, elevations, and perspectives — through which buildings are conceived and communicated.

name: Floor Plans
description: Two-dimensional horizontal cuts showing room layout, circulation, and spatial relationships.

name: Sections
description: Vertical cuts through a building revealing structure, floor levels, and spatial sequence.

name: Elevations
description: Orthographic views of a building's facades showing proportion, materials, and openings.

name: Perspective Rendering
description: Three-dimensional representations conveying how a design will appear to the eye.

name: Physical Modeling
description: Scaled three-dimensional models in wood, cardboard, or 3D printing for design study and presentation.

name: Architectural Elements
description: The constituent parts of buildings — columns, arches, vaults, domes, facades, and ornament — that define architectural language.

name: Column Orders
description: The classical systems of columns — Doric, Ionic, Corinthian, and Tuscan — governing proportion and decoration.

name: Arch & Vault
description: Curved structural forms — barrel, groin, rib — that span openings and define Romanesque and Gothic space.

name: Dome
description: Hemispherical roofing structures, from the Pantheon to Islamic and Byzantine domes, symbolizing cosmic order.

name: Facade Composition
description: The ordering of a building's exterior — rhythm, proportion, fenestration, and hierarchy.

name: Ornamentation
description: Decorative detailing — moldings, friezes, tracery, and sculpture — that carries cultural and symbolic meaning.

name: Branding & Identity
description: Creating visual identity systems — logos, color, typography — that define an organization's public face.

name: Typography
description: The art of designing and arranging letterforms for legibility, tone, and expression.

name: Packaging Design
description: Designing containers and labels that protect products and communicate brand at the point of sale.

name: Editorial Design
description: Layout of books, magazines, and digital publications — grids, hierarchy, and image-text relationships.

name: Haute Couture
description: Made-to-measure, hand-finished fashion at the highest craft level, governed by the Chambre Syndicale in Paris.

name: Ready-to-Wear
description: Factory-produced designer clothing in standard sizes — the commercial core of the fashion industry.

name: Textile Design
description: Designing woven, knitted, and printed fabrics — patterns, fibers, and surface treatments for fashion and interiors.
